race.description:
Undead freed from eternal servitude, forever looking for purpose and home.

An animated figure made of dry bones devoid of flesh and muscle, you were likely raised by necromantic caster or dark, supernatural curse as a simple minion, completely without will and self knowledge. something changed, however; perhaps your master was slain, the land cleansed, or your merely awoke one day to fragmented memories of your previous life. whatever the case, possessed of a fragmented sense of self and newfound purpose, you struck out into the wider world to find a new destiny.
race.longDescription: An animated figure made of dry bones devoid of flesh and muscle, you were likely raised by necromantic caster or dark, supernatural curse as a simple minion, completely without will and self knowledge. something changed, however; perhaps your master was slain, the land cleansed, or your merely awoke one day to fragmented memories of your previous life. whatever the case, possessed of a fragmented sense of self and newfound purpose, you struck out into the wider world to find a new destiny.

definition.name: Ability Score Increase
definition.description: Your Constitution score is increased by 1.
definition.snippet: Your Constitution score is increased by 1.

definition.name: Dead Immortality
definition.description: You do not age, given time the necrotic energies that sustain you will heal most wounds you take at approximately the same rate as a mortal, and your hit dice function as normal.
definition.snippet: You do not age, given time the necrotic energies that sustain you will heal most wounds you take at approximately the same rate as a mortal, and your hit dice function as normal.

definition.name: Past Life
definition.description: Choose another living race besides this one. Before your death you were a member of this race and appear as an undead version of it. your size, height, and movement speed are the same as a typical member of that race. you do not retain special movement (Swimming, Flying), and, though you may choose to have formerly been member of a sub-race of a particular race, you derive no benefits from doing so.
definition.snippet: You were once a member of another race before being undead.

definition.name: Undead
definition.description: Raised from the dead as a being of undeath, you count as an undead creature for all spells and abilities that affect the undead. You are immune to disease and treat exhaustion as if it was one level less. you do not need to eat or breathe, but you can ingest food and drink if you wish. instead of sleeping, you enter an inactive state for 4 hours each day. you do not dream in this state; you are fully aware of your surroundings and notice approaching enemies and other events as normal.
definition.snippet: You are DEAD

definition.name: Darkvision
definition.description: Through the necromantic energy animating you, you are able to perceive with greater clarity that which lurks in the darkness. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. you can't discern colour in darkness, only shades of grey.
definition.snippet: You can see 60 feet in dim light, and in darkness you can see 60 feet in shades of grey.

definition.name: Ability Score Increase.
definition.description: Your Dexterity or Intelligence Score is increased by 2.
definition.snippet: Your Dexterity or Intelligence Score is increased by 2.

definition.name: Bone Pile
definition.description: When you are reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, you can drop 1 hit point instead. if you do, you reduce yourself to a pile of bones, render yourself prone, and are considered to be under a similar effect to the feign death spell. while subject to this condition, you are unable to move or take actions other than using an action to end this effect. you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
definition.snippet: You are made of bones

definition.name: Bone to Pick
definition.description: Whenever both of your hands are free (not including equipped shields), you may choose to use a free hand and a bonus action to remove an arm, and a bonus action to remove one of your hands or arms. if you remove an arm, it counts as a weapon with finesse property that deals 1d8 bludgeoning damage, and you have proficiency with your arm while you wield it. if you remove a hand, it counts as thieves' tools or a similar set of simple tools while you hold it. in either case, removed hands and arms may be re-attached by using another bonus action.
definition.snippet: You are made from bone, allowing you to do some certain actions.

definition.name: Shield
definition.description: Shields require the Utilize action to Don or Doff. You gain the Armor Class benefit of a Shield only if you have training with it.

definition.name: Chain Mail
definition.description: Made of interlocking metal rings, chain mail includes a layer of quilted fabric worn underneath the mail to prevent chafing and to cushion the impact of blows. The suit includes gauntlets.

definition.name: Javelin
definition.description:
Proficiency with a Javelin allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it.

This weapon has the following mastery property. To use this property, you must have a feature that lets you use it.

Slow. If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn’t exceed 10 feet.

properties.name: Thrown
properties.description: If a weapon has the Thrown property, you can throw the weapon to make a ranged attack, and you can draw that weapon as part of the attack. If the weapon is a Melee weapon, use the same ability modifier for the attack and damage rolls that you use for a melee attack with that weapon.

properties.name: Slow
properties.description: If you hit a creature with this weapon and deal damage to it, you can reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of your next turn. If the creature is hit more than once by weapons that have this property, the Speed reduction doesn't exceed 10 feet.

definition.name: Mace
definition.description:
Proficiency with a Mace allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it.

This weapon has the following mastery property. To use this property, you must have a feature that lets you use it.

Sap. If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

properties.name: Sap
properties.description: If you hit a creature with this weapon, that creature has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

definition.name: Backpack
definition.description:
A backpack is a leather pack carried on the back, typically with straps to secure it. A backpack can hold 1 cubic foot/ 30 pounds of gear.

You can also strap items, such as a bedroll or a coil of rope, to the outside of a backpack.

definition.name: Bedroll
definition.description: You never know where you’re going to sleep, and a bedroll helps you get better sleep in a hayloft or on the cold ground. A bedroll consists of bedding and a blanket thin enough to be rolled up and tied. In an emergency, it can double as a stretcher.

definition.name: Mess Kit
definition.description: This tin box contains a cup and simple cutlery. The box clamps together, and one side can be used as a cooking pan and the other as a plate or shallow bowl.

definition.name: Rations (1 day)
definition.description: Rations consist of dry foods suitable for extended travel, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts.

definition.name: Rope, Hempen (50 feet)
definition.description: Rope, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

definition.name: Tinderbox
definition.description: This small container holds flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a torch -- or anything else with abundant, exposed fuel -- takes an action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.

definition.name: Torch
definition.description: A torch burns for 1 hour, providing bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a burning torch and hit, it deals 1 fire damage.

definition.name: Waterskin
definition.description: A waterskin can hold 4 pints of liquid.

definition.name: Holy Symbol
definition.description: A holy symbol is a representation of a god or pantheon. A cleric or paladin can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus, as described in the Spellcasting section. To use the symbol in this way, the caster must hold it in hand, wear it visibly, or bear it on a shield.

definition.name: Cleric
definition.description:
A priestly champion who wields divine magic in service of a higher power

Hit Die: d8
Primary Ability: Wisdom
Saves: Wisdom & Charisma
definition.equipmentDescription:
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a mace or (b) a warhammer (if proficient)
  • (a) scale mail, (b) leather armor, or (c) chain mail (if proficient)
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) any simple weapon
  • (a) a priest’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack
  • A shield and a holy symbol

classFeatures.name: Spellcasting
classFeatures.description:
As a conduit for divine power, you can cast cleric spells. See Spells Rules for the general rules of spellcasting and the Spells Listing for the cleric spell list.

Cantrips

At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the cleric spell list. You learn additional cleric cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Cleric table.

Preparing and Casting Spells

The Cleric table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your cleric spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell’s level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of cleric spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the cleric spell list. When you do so, choose a number of cleric spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your cleric level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

For example, if you are a 3rd-level cleric, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With a Wisdom of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination. If you prepare the 1st-level spell cure wounds, you can cast it using a 1st-level or 2nd-level slot. Casting the spell doesn’t remove it from your list of prepared spells.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of cleric spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

Spellcasting Ability

Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your cleric spells. The power of your spells comes from your devotion to your deity. You use your Wisdom whenever a cleric spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a cleric spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

Ritual Casting

You can cast a cleric spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell prepared.

Spellcasting Focus

You can use a holy symbol (see the Adventuring Gear section) as a spellcasting focus for your cleric spells.
classFeatures.summary: Cast spells through prayer and meditation.

classFeatures.name: Divine Domain
classFeatures.description:
Choose one domain related to your deity. Your choice grants you domain spells and other features when you choose it at 1st level. It also grants you additional ways to use Channel Divinity when you gain that feature at 2nd level, and additional benefits at 6th, 8th, and 17th levels.

Domain Spells

Each domain has a list of spells — its domain spells — that you gain at the cleric levels noted in the domain description. Once you gain a domain spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn’t count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.

If you have a domain spell that doesn’t appear on the cleric spell list, the spell is nonetheless a cleric spell for you.
classFeatures.summary: Choose one aspect of your deity’s portfolio to emphasize, and gain powers related to it.

classFeatures.name: Channel Divinity
classFeatures.description:
At 2nd level, you gain the ability to channel divine energy directly from your deity, using that energy to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Turn Undead and an effect determined by your domain. Some domains grant you additional effects as you advance in levels, as noted in the domain description.

When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which effect to create. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Channel Divinity again.

Some Channel Divinity effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your cleric spell save DC.

Beginning at 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity twice between rests, and beginning at 18th level, you can use it three times between rests. When you finish a short or long rest, you regain your expended uses.

Channel Divinity: Turn Undead

As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring the undead. Each undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can’t willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can’t take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there’s nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.

classFeatures.name: Ability Score Improvement
classFeatures.description:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

classFeatures.name: Destroy Undead
classFeatures.description:
Starting at 5th level, when an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, the creature is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold, as shown in the Destroy Undead table.

Destroy Undead
Cleric Level Destroys Undead of CR …
5th 1/2 or lower
8th 1 or lower
11th 2 or lower
14th 3 or lower
17th 4 or lower

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

classFeatures.name: Divine Intervention
classFeatures.description:
Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.

Imploring your deity’s aid requires you to use your action. Describe the assistance you seek, and roll percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your cleric level, your deity intervenes. The DM chooses the nature of the intervention; the effect of any cleric spell or cleric domain spell would be appropriate.

If your deity intervenes, you can’t use this feature again for 7 days. Otherwise, you can use it again after you finish a long rest.

At 20th level, your call for intervention succeeds automatically, no roll required.

classFeatures.name: Proficiencies
classFeatures.description:
Armor: Light armor, medium armor, shields
Weapons: Simple weapons
Tools: None
Saving Throws: Wisdom, Charisma
Skills: Choose two from History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion

classFeatures.name: Hit Points
classFeatures.description:
Hit Dice: 1d8 per cleric level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per cleric level after 1st

definition.tagline: A Miraculous Priest of Divine Power
definition.cardDescription: Clerics draw power from the realms of the gods and harness it to work miracles.
definition.highlights:
• Invoke divine magic to bolster people and battle foes.
  • Channel divine energy to heal allies or sear enemies.
  • Martial the power of the gods to ward off Undead.
definition.iconicGear:
• A Holy Symbol borne prominently
  • Cloth vestments worn over a Chain shirt
  • Necklace of Prayer Beads

subclassDefinition.name: Undeath Domain
subclassDefinition.description: The Undeath Domain focuses on the grim negative, energy of death - one of the many forces of the universe - that sustains all undead creatures.

classFeatures.name: Bonus Proficiency
classFeatures.description: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with the Stealth skill, can communicate simple ideas with undead creatures, and gain Undercommon as a language.

classFeatures.name: Disciple of Undeath
classFeatures.description: Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to damage a Creature, you can target up to one other creature who then takes 2 + the spell’s level damage as Necrotic.

classFeatures.name: Channel Divinity: Disrupt Life
classFeatures.description:
Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to harm the already injured.

As an action, you present your Unholy Symbol and evoke Harming energy that can remove a number of Hit Points equal to 5 times your cleric level. Choose any number of creatures within 30 feet of you, and divide the damage among them. This feature cannot outright kill a creature, but it can reduce them to 0 Hit Points. You can’t use this feature on Undead or Fiends.

classFeatures.name: Cursed Destroyer
classFeatures.description: Beginning at 6th level, the Harming spells you cast on others heal you even more. When you Cast a Spell of 1st level or higher that Removes Hit Points from a creature other than you, you regain Hit Points equal to 2 + the spell’s level.

classFeatures.name: Ghastly Strike
classFeatures.description: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with unholy energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon Attack, you can cause the Attack to deal an extra 1d8 Necrotic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

classFeatures.name: Elite Death Dealer
classFeatures.description: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to Damage a creature with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of dealing 3d10 damage to a creature, you’d deal 30 damage. Additionally, you are also immune to Necrotic damage.

classFeatures.name: Domain Spells
classFeatures.description:
Undeath Domain Spells:

1st: Bane, Inflict Wounds

3rd: Lesser Curse*, Spiritual Weapon

5th: Beacon of Despair*, Animate Dead

7th: Death Call*, Guardian of Faith

9th: Mass Life Drain*, Raise Dead

*=Homebrew

definition.snippet: Starting at 1st level, and again at 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level your Domain grants you certain spells.

definition.name: Spellcasting
definition.description:
As a conduit for divine power, you can cast cleric spells. See Spells Rules for the general rules of spellcasting and the Spells Listing for the cleric spell list.

Cantrips

At 1st level, you know three cantrips of your choice from the cleric spell list. You learn additional cleric cantrips of your choice at higher levels, as shown in the Cantrips Known column of the Cleric table.

Preparing and Casting Spells

The Cleric table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your cleric spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell’s level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

You prepare the list of cleric spells that are available for you to cast, choosing from the cleric spell list. When you do so, choose a number of cleric spells equal to your Wisdom modifier + your cleric level (minimum of one spell). The spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

For example, if you are a 3rd-level cleric, you have four 1st-level and two 2nd-level spell slots. With a Wisdom of 16, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of 1st or 2nd level, in any combination. If you prepare the 1st-level spell cure wounds, you can cast it using a 1st-level or 2nd-level slot. Casting the spell doesn’t remove it from your list of prepared spells.

You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest. Preparing a new list of cleric spells requires time spent in prayer and meditation: at least 1 minute per spell level for each spell on your list.

Spellcasting Ability

Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your cleric spells. The power of your spells comes from your devotion to your deity. You use your Wisdom whenever a cleric spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a cleric spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier

Ritual Casting

You can cast a cleric spell as a ritual if that spell has the ritual tag and you have the spell prepared.

Spellcasting Focus

You can use a holy symbol (see the Adventuring Gear section) as a spellcasting focus for your cleric spells.
definition.snippet: You can cast prepared cleric spells using WIS as your spellcasting modifier (Spell DC {{savedc:wis}}, Spell Attack {{spellattack:wis}}) and prepared cleric spells as rituals if they have the ritual tag. You can use a holy symbol as a spellcasting focus.

definition.name: Divine Domain
definition.description:
Choose one domain related to your deity. Your choice grants you domain spells and other features when you choose it at 1st level. It also grants you additional ways to use Channel Divinity when you gain that feature at 2nd level, and additional benefits at 6th, 8th, and 17th levels.

Domain Spells

Each domain has a list of spells — its domain spells — that you gain at the cleric levels noted in the domain description. Once you gain a domain spell, you always have it prepared, and it doesn’t count against the number of spells you can prepare each day.

If you have a domain spell that doesn’t appear on the cleric spell list, the spell is nonetheless a cleric spell for you.
definition.snippet: You choose a divine domain that grants you additional spells and other features related to your deity.

definition.name: Channel Divinity
definition.description:
At 2nd level, you gain the ability to channel divine energy directly from your deity, using that energy to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Turn Undead and an effect determined by your domain. Some domains grant you additional effects as you advance in levels, as noted in the domain description.

When you use your Channel Divinity, you choose which effect to create. You must then finish a short or long rest to use your Channel Divinity again.

Some Channel Divinity effects require saving throws. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your cleric spell save DC.

Beginning at 6th level, you can use your Channel Divinity twice between rests, and beginning at 18th level, you can use it three times between rests. When you finish a short or long rest, you regain your expended uses.

Channel Divinity: Turn Undead

As an action, you present your holy symbol and speak a prayer censuring the undead. Each undead that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

A turned creature must spend its turns trying to move as far away from you as it can, and it can’t willingly move to a space within 30 feet of you. It also can’t take reactions. For its action, it can use only the Dash action or try to escape from an effect that prevents it from moving. If there’s nowhere to move, the creature can use the Dodge action.
definition.snippet: You can channel divine energy to fuel magical effects a number of times per short rest

definition.name: Ability Score Improvement
definition.description:
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Using the optional feats rule, you can forgo taking this feature to take a feat of your choice instead.

definition.name: Destroy Undead
definition.description:
Starting at 5th level, when an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, the creature is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold, as shown in the Destroy Undead table.

Destroy Undead
Cleric Level Destroys Undead of CR …
5th 1/2 or lower
8th 1 or lower
11th 2 or lower
14th 3 or lower
17th 4 or lower
definition.snippet: When an undead fails its saving throw against your Turn Undead feature, it is instantly destroyed if its CR is lower than the threshold for your level.

definition.name: Divine Intervention
definition.description:
Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.

Imploring your deity’s aid requires you to use your action. Describe the assistance you seek, and roll percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your cleric level, your deity intervenes. The DM chooses the nature of the intervention; the effect of any cleric spell or cleric domain spell would be appropriate.

If your deity intervenes, you can’t use this feature again for 7 days. Otherwise, you can use it again after you finish a long rest.

At 20th level, your call for intervention succeeds automatically, no roll required.
definition.snippet:
As an action, you can request your deity's aid and roll percentile dice. If your roll is equal to or less than {{classlevel}}, your deity intervenes (your DM chooses the nature of the intervention). If successful, you can't use this feature again for 7 days, otherwise, you can use it again after a long rest. 

At 20th level, your request succeeds automatically, no roll required.

definition.name: Proficiencies
definition.description:
Armor: Light armor, medium armor, shields
Weapons: Simple weapons
Tools: None
Saving Throws: Wisdom, Charisma
Skills: Choose two from History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, and Religion

definition.name: Hit Points
definition.description:
Hit Dice: 1d8 per cleric level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per cleric level after 1st

definition.name: Equipment
definition.description:
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

  • (a) a mace or (b) a warhammer (if proficient)
  • (a) scale mail, (b) leather armor, or (c) chain mail (if proficient)
  • (a) a light crossbow and 20 bolts or (b) any simple weapon
  • (a) a priest’s pack or (b) an explorer’s pack
  • A shield and a holy symbol

class.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
class.snippet: As an action, you can use Channel Divinity and present your holy symbol to restore up to {{classlevel*5#unsigned}} HP divided among any creatures within 30 ft. up to half a creature's HP max. You can’t use this feature on an undead or a construct.

class.name: Harness Divine Power
class.description:
2nd-level cleric feature
You can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to fuel your spells. As a bonus action, you touch your holy symbol, utter a prayer, and regain one expended spell slot, the level of which can be no higher than half your proficiency bonus (rounded up). The number of times you can use this feature is based on the level you’ve reached in this class: 2nd level, once; 6th level, twice; and 18th level, thrice. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
class.snippet: You can expend a use of your Channel Divinity to fuel your spells. As a bonus action, you regain one expended spell slot of up to level {{(proficiency/2)@roundup#unsigned}}. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

definition.name: Mending
definition.description:
This spell repairs a single break or tear in an object you touch, such as a broken chain link, two halves of a broken key, a torn cloak, or a leaking wineskin. As long as the break or tear is no larger than 1 foot in any dimension, you mend it, leaving no trace of the former damage.

This spell can physically repair a magic item or construct, but the spell can't restore magic to such an object.

definition.name: Sacred Flame
definition.description:
Flame-like radiance descends on a creature that you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d8 radiant damage. The target gains no benefit from cover for this saving throw.

The spell's damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8), and 17th level (4d8).

definition.name: Spare the Dying
definition.description: You touch a living creature that has 0 hit points. The creature becomes stable. This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.

definition.name: Guiding Bolt
definition.description:
A flash of light streaks toward a creature of your choice within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 4d6 radiant damage, and the next attack roll made against this target before the end of your next turn has advantage, thanks to the mystical dim light glittering on the target until then.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

definition.name: Healing Word
definition.description:
A creature of your choice that you can see within range regains hit points equal to 1d4 + your spellcasting ability modifier. This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the healing increases by 1d4 for each slot level above 1st.

definition.name: Shield of Faith
definition.description: A shimmering field appears and surrounds a creature of your choice within range, granting it a +2 bonus to AC for the duration.
definition.componentsDescription: a small parchment with a bit of holy text written on it

definition.name: Prayer of Healing
definition.description:
Up to six creatures of your choice that you can see within range each regain hit points equal to 2d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the healing increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

definition.name: Cure Wounds
definition.description:
A creature you touch regains a number of hit points equal to 1d8 + your spellcasting ability modifier. This spell has no effect on undead or constructs.

At Higher Levels. When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the healing increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 1st.

definition.name: Light
definition.description:
You touch one object that is no larger than 10 feet in any dimension. Until the spell ends, the object sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. The light can be colored as you like. Completely covering the object with something opaque blocks the light. The spell ends if you cast it again or dismiss it as an action.

If you target an object held or worn by a hostile creature, that creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw to avoid the spell.
